title: London session of the USD bond market recommended closed all day for New Year's Day — the one day of the turn-of-year corridor on which London, Tokyo and New York are all shut together
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 299,272 bytes) and parsed panel by panel, with region attribution fixed to the page's own 'U.S. / U.K. / Japan Holiday Recommendations' headings rather than to card order. The U.K. panel's last 2026/2027 card reads exactly ['New Year's Day 2026/2027', 'Friday, January 1, 2027'] with NO early-close note attached — the full-closure shape, distinct from the 'Early Close (…)' entries elsewhere on the same page. Filed estimate on the same three counts as every sifma-* entry already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an industry trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and SIFMA's own page states its schedule is a recommendation ('On behalf of financial markets participants, SIFMA recommends a holiday schedule for financial markets in the U.S., U.K. and Japan') rather than a market-wide halt each firm is bound by. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED by the new-years-day-market-closure-2027-01-01 initial research (2026-09-09), found inside its own corridor while parsing all three SIFMA panels for the US card. It follows the exact precedent this calendar already set with sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2026-12-28 and -2027-03-29: SIFMA's three regional panels are three TIME ZONES of one US-dollar bond market, not three asset classes, so a U.K.-panel full close is its own tracked entry rather than a restatement of the US one. WHY IT EARNS A ROW RATHER THAN A LINE IN THE PROPOSER'S LEDGER: the turn-of-year corridor is the one stretch where that single dollar market visibly desynchronizes and then re-synchronizes, and only a per-region entry can carry the shape. On 2026-12-28 London is dark, Tokyo closes early and New York runs a full session (already tracked). On 2026-12-31 New York equities run a FULL session, US fixed income closes early at 2:00 p.m. ET, and Tokyo is fully shut on a SIFMA 'Bank Holiday' card — the maximum desync of the corridor. On 2027-01-01 all three are shut together, and MEASURED THIS SESSION against the page's own panels, that is the norm rather than the exception: all 12 US-panel full closes across 2026 and 2027-01-01 are also full closes on the U.K. and Japan panels, so the tri-market shutdown is NOT what distinguishes this date. What distinguishes it is that it terminates the desync — it is the wall the 2026-12-31 triple runs into. HONEST LIMIT, inherited from the sibling U.K. entry's own research and not re-derived here: gov.uk dates a statutory England-and-Wales bank holiday on 2027-01-01 too, so London is dark whatever SIFMA recommends and this card is redundant with statute — the opposite of sifma-bond-market-closure-2026-10-12 / -2026-11-11, where NYSE trades a full session and the SIFMA card IS the information. Low impact accordingly. A NAMING GAP DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN: SIFMA's Japan panel carries the same 2027-01-01 full close AND a 'Bank Holiday / Thursday, December 31, 2026', neither of which is proposed here, because this calendar has a sifma-japan-early-close-* precedent and no sifma-japan-*-closure-* one, and inventing a naming scheme in a proposal is how two lanes end up with two slugs for one event. The 12-31 Japan bond closure is separately noted in the proposer's ledger; jpx-market-closure-2026-12-31 already tracks the equity side of that date.
